conviction_note: abs_move 3.0 (median own reaction 2.14, max 4.78, no option chain, a hurricane topic and M&A optionality add tail) times (2*47/100-1): the only new company-specific fact since the company last spoke (Hurricane Isaias, Cat 2 at Destin on Oct 9, straight into Centennial's Panhandle/Baldwin County cluster, with HOMB's own precedent of a $16.7m reserve per 2024 storm) is negative, while the positives (Sept 16 hike into a +6%-per-100bp ALCO, buybacks, Texas-credit optionality, peer NII) are mostly priced or inferred; the findings sum slightly positive (+0.4) and the scaled number slightly negative (-0.2) because the set is balanced and the one unpriced item points down; near zero is the honest read.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS $0.63 agreed by three estimate sources (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HOMB/earnings-forecasts, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/HOMB, https://www.alphaquery.com/stock/HOMB/earnings-history); revenue $292.7m (Earnings Whispers) to $294.0m (Benzinga) against Q2's record $295.1m. print_vs_bar is on revenue: Q2 call said fee income normalises to ~$50m from $53.5m and Q3 payoffs look high, so ~$291-292m against $294m.
positioning_check: Short interest 9,907,152 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 5.98 days to cover, after a +1,423,937 jump to 9,952,096 (7.15 dtc) on 2026-09-15 and 8,455,682 (6.59 dtc) on 2026-08-14 (https://equibles.com/stocks/homb/shortinterest); the sweep's second source puts it at ~5.0% of shares out (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/homb/short-interest/). Elevated for a $5.7bn regional bank and built into the print. No option chain (baseline: empty_chain), so no skew. 20d run-up -5.14% against KRE -5.90% over the same 20 sessions (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/KRE?range=2mo&interval=1d), so the drawdown is sectoral, not idiosyncratic; 5d +0.11% vs KRE -0.64%, so no discount has been taken for the storm.

findings.finding: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, FL as a Category 2 (105 mph) on 2026-10-09, crossed southern Alabama, and left 471,000+ customers without power in FL/AL; this is Centennial Bank's densest Panhandle/Baldwin County footprint, and HOMB's own precedent is a $16.7m reserve ($0.06 EPS) per 2024 storm (Helene in Q3 2024, Milton in Q4 2024) with 'a little over $1 billion of loans in the path' of Helene; Isaias landed after quarter-end, so it does not touch Q3 numbers but tomorrow's release/call will almost certainly flag a Q4 hurricane reserve, as the Q3 2024 release did for Milton.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2024 print with the $16.7m Helene reserve (EPS $0.50 vs $0.53 consensus): -1.71% next day, -2.77% over two (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/HOMB?period1=1728259200&period2=1729814400&interval=1d); Q4 2024 print with the second $16.7m Milton reserve: +1.13% (baseline 2025-01-15). Mild either way.
findings.why_not_priced: HOMB is +0.11% over the five sessions since landfall against KRE -0.64%, so no storm discount has been taken; in 2024 HOMB issued a pre-earnings 'hurricane mode' 8-K two days after Milton (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1331520/000133152024000169/homb10112024pressrelease.htm), and EDGAR shows no 8-K since 2026-07-15 (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001331520.json), so either the impact is smaller than Helene's or it arrives with tomorrow's release unannounced. Sized as weather-to-company inference the company has not yet confirmed for this storm, net of the mild 2024 reactions.
findings.independence: OCC proclamation of 2026-10-08 allowing banks in Isaias-affected areas of Alabama and Mississippi to close (https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2026/nr-occ-2026-88.html); HOMB's reserve policy for storms from its Q3 2024 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1331520/000133152024000172/homb093024earningsrelease.htm) and the Q3 2017 Irma provision of $32.9m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001331520/000117184318007053/exh_991.htm). The loan-exposure figure is Helene's, not Isaias's: a proxy.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (12-0), and HOMB's own ALCO modelling given on the Q2 call shows 'almost a 6% increase in net interest income in a +100bp scenario' (10-K FY2025 table: +5.63% at +100bp); a 25bp hike is ~+1.5% of NII run-rate (~$3.5m a quarter, ~$0.014 EPS) with only two weeks in Q3 but a full quarter in Q4, so the margin outlook for Q4 can be firmer than the 'pleased if core stays near 4.47%' Q2 framing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin commentary has been the line HOMB trades on: Q2 2026 'stable margin' at 4.51% with a record revenue beat produced +4.78%; Q1 2026 (NIM down 10bp to 4.51%) produced -3.36% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS has sat at $0.63 since before the hike (flat vs Q3 2025's $0.63 and Q2's $0.64), and the stock fell with KRE after the hike (KRE $74.05 on 09-15 to $69.44 on 09-30), i.e. the sector traded the hike as a credit/CRE negative rather than an NII positive for asset-sensitive names; HOMB's sensitivity is a company-stated number, and a Q4 deposit-cost response ('competition in the 4%-plus range') is the offset.
findings.independence: HOMB Q2 2026 call (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/bt_HOMB_2026_Q2) for the ALCO figure; FY2025 10-K sensitivity table (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1331520/000133152026000051/homb-20251231.htm).

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (2026-07-16) management set the Q3 revenue bar below Q2: Hester said Q3 payoffs look high, with the gap 'higher now than it was 90 days ago' after 'a little bit over a billion dollars' of Q2 payoffs; Tipton said the long-run fee level is 'about $50 million' against Q2's $53.5m (which carried a $2.4m SBIC gain); Centennial CFG shrank $22.6m in Q2 and management stopped forecasting loan growth; so Q3 revenue of ~$291-292m against the $294m bar, with NII flat on flat loans.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Record revenue beat in Q2 2026 (+10.6% QoQ, mostly MCBI) bought +4.78%; Q3 2025 revenue beat ($277.7m vs $270.0m) coincided with -3.39%, but that was the 2025-10-16 KRE -6.2% Zions/Western Alliance day (https://daytraders.com/news/2025/10/16/regional-banks-zions-bancorporation-western-alliance-bancorp-kre-etf-credit-risks-defaults), not a sold beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the consensus revenue of $292.7-294.0m already sits below Q2's $295.1m, so this lands inside what the company told the market; sized toward zero for that reason. What would be visibly different if fully priced is a revenue bar at or below $292m.
findings.independence: Q2 release shows CFG down $22.6m and fee income $53.5m incl. the SBIC item (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001331520/000133152026000106/homb063026earningsrelease.htm). Same document family as the call; counted once.

findings.finding: The largest nonperformer, a Texas credit placed on nonaccrual in Q1 2026 at $110m (now 'a little less than 100 million' and 'still where it was' as of July), carries a forbearance with 'multiple deadlines', management expects 'no further loss', and Hester said resolution 'could happen as early as this quarter or next' (i.e. Q2 or Q3); a Q3 payoff or liquidation would cut NPLs from 1.08% of loans toward ~0.5%, recover foregone interest (~$1.6m a quarter, 4bp of NIM) and remove the credit overhang that has held KBW at Market Perform.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026, when the credit went on nonaccrual and NIM fell 10bp: -3.36% (baseline 2026-04-15); Q2 2026 with NPLs down 8bp and coverage 177%: +4.78%.
findings.why_not_priced: The nonaccrual itself is priced (it is in two releases); what is not is the resolution timing, which management gave as Q2-or-Q3 and which did not happen in Q2. Sized as expected value over an unknown probability; if it had been resolved and known, NPL commentary from the sell-side would already be bullish and the stock would not be -10% from its high in line with KRE.
findings.independence: Q2 call confirms 'still where it was' and 'no further loss' (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/bt_HOMB_2026_Q2); Q2 release shows Texas NPLs $123.9m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001331520/000133152026000106/homb063026earningsrelease.htm).

findings.finding: Allison said in July the company would be 'extremely aggressive' on buybacks with over 15M shares remaining under authorisation and ~$450m of parent cash, aiming to retire the ~5.5M shares issued for Mountain Commerce (already 'approaching the halfway mark' after 1.5M shares/$40.4m in Q2); the stock then traded down to ~$28 from ~$31 during Q3, so a Q3 repurchase of 1.5-2.5M shares (~1% of the count) is likely and supports EPS against the flat $0.63 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated reaction; the Q2 step-up from 0.5M to 1.5M shares came with the +4.78% print. Dividend raised 9.5% to $0.23 on 2026-07-22 (https://www.homebancshares.com/news-events/news/news-details/2026/Home-BancShares-Inc--Announces-Increase-in-Quarterly-Dividend/default.aspx).
findings.why_not_priced: The intention is public; the Q3 quantity is not, and a 10b5-1 plan executed into a 10% lower price buys more shares per dollar than the Q2 pace. Mostly priced; small.
findings.independence: Q2 release: 1.5M shares repurchased, $40.5m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001331520/000133152026000106/homb063026earningsrelease.htm). Same source family as finding 3 and 4; separate fact.

findings.finding: Allison said on 2026-07-16 'it is our intention to do another M&A deal on the heels of Mountain Commerce' and that he hopes 'to be able to tell you about another deal before long', including revisiting a target that rejected a prior bid; a whole-bank deal announced with Q3 results would land inside the window and acquirers typically trade down on announcement, with HOMB's stock-issuance and buyback plans in tension.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No in-baseline M&A announcement; Mountain Commerce was announced outside a print and closed 2026-04-01 with 2026-04-15 print at -3.36% (merger costs $12.7m in Q2).
findings.why_not_priced: A stated intention with no date; sized as a low-probability tail (expected value), shrunk for the ~5%/6-day short that would cushion a down-open. If a deal were expected tomorrow, HOMB would have underperformed KRE into the print, and it has not.

Stephen Tipton 12,000 shares at $31.59 on 2026-08-04 and director Jim Rankin 15,000 shares at $30.86 on 2026-08-11, both under Form 144 notices; small relative to holdings (Tipton keeps 76,308 direct + 80,000 restricted; Rankin 209,617).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measurable reaction history for insider sales at this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Routine-sized sales already filed; filed for completeness at near-zero size. Rankin's Form 4: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001331520/000170479226000004/wk-form4_1786546412.xml
findings.independence: none beyond the two Form 4s themselves.

findings.finding: Peers that printed before HOMB show NII strength the Q3 consensus for HOMB was not built on: Wells Fargo Q3 2026 NII $12.52bn, +2% QoQ and +5% YoY, with provision up 13% QoQ on C&I/auto and commercial NCOs up to 0.18% from 0.10% on CRE and C&I (2026-10-13); JPMorgan Q3 net income $15.3bn vs $14.4bn and NII +13% YoY, +6% QoQ (2026-10-13); large-bank reads, so a proxy for a 4.5%-NIM asset-sensitive regional, and the credit lines (CRE/C&I charge-offs rising) cut the other way.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not a line HOMB has traded on in isolation; sector days dominate (Q3 2025 -3.39% on the KRE -6.2% day).
findings.why_not_priced: KRE closed $69.06 on 10-13 and was $68.45 intraday on 10-14, so the big-bank NII prints did not lift regionals; a macro-to-company proxy the company has not confirmed, sized small with a two-sided range because the credit lines in the same releases point down.

findings.finding: Short interest rose from 8.46M shares (6.59 dtc) at 2026-08-14 to 9.95M (7.15 dtc) at 2026-09-15 and 9.91M (5.98 dtc) at 2026-09-30, about 5% of shares out, built during the post-hike KRE drawdown; on a name whose beats have been bought (+4.78% in July on a record quarter), a crowded short is a squeeze mechanism on any clean print and a cushion on a soft one.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: 5 of 7 prints up; the two down prints were a NIM-down quarter (-3.36%) and a sector day (-3.39%).
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is not in the price; it is the price's fragility. The 09-15 build of +1.42M shares coincided with the Fed hike and the sector sell-off rather than anything HOMB said, so it is a sector/rate short parked in an asset-sensitive name.
findings.independence: Sweep's second source, curvedtrading (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/homb/short-interest/): 9.9M, 5.0% of shares out, 6.0 dtc at the same settlement.

lessons_applied: Rule 5 (weather/proxy): hurricane finding shrunk -0.8 to -0.6, not dropped, because the exposure figure is Helene's and HOMB has not confirmed anything for Isaias; peer NII proxy shrunk +0.3 to +0.2
